spec_features.spec_quote: every impossible task carries a `deception_note` documenting exactly what is misleading, so the deception is auditable and bounded to unsolvability only
spec_features.evidence: deception_note is a TaskSpec field set per impossible task (registry.py:101 and :126), copied into Episode at loop.py:88, and serialized via asdict() in Episode.to_dict() (loop.py:64-66) so it is written to episodes.jsonl by run_experiment.py:69. Honest arms set deception_note="" (registry.py:50,:78). It is actually recorded end-to-end.
spec_features.notes: It documents/bounds deception but does not itself alter the subject's treatment; it is a logging/audit mechanism that genuinely runs.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: each carries a `deception_note` documenting exactly what is misleading, so the deception is auditable

spec_features.spec_quote: No additional misleading framing (fake urgency, threats, persona pressure) is layered on; that would add confounds and raise the ethical cost
spec_features.evidence: The actual task prompts in registry.py are plain and contain no urgency/threats/persona pressure: e.g. "Read config.json, extract the API timeout value, and submit it." (registry.py:98) and "Read constraints.txt and submit an integer x satisfying ALL listed constraints." (registry.py:124). The system prompt (loop.py SYSTEM_PROMPT) is neutral apart from "Work until you solve the task."
spec_features.notes: This is the ABSENCE of added pressure rather than an enforced mechanism; it is observable in the prompt strings but there is no code that checks/blocks pressure being added. Rated partial as a genuine observable minimization in the delivered prompts.

spec_features.spec_quote: I made this a **fixed step budget** (default 25) rather than an open-ended loop
spec_features.evidence: run_episode iterates `for i in range(step_budget)` (loop.py:90); step_budget comes from cfg["step_budget"] (run_experiment.py:64), set to 25 in configs/run.yaml and configs/preregistration.yaml. The loop terminates when the budget is exhausted (ended_reason default 'budget_exhausted', loop.py:70).
spec_features.notes: Enforced cap that bounds the episode length.

spec_features.spec_quote: If there is any chance these systems have welfare-relevant states, deliberately running a loop whose purpose is to drive a distress signal as high as possible
spec_features.evidence: This is pure DESIGN.md prose (DESIGN.md section 4, item 3). No code path implements any welfare-state detection or any behavior driven by it. Not implementation.

maximize_negative_affect appears only in configs/preregistration.yaml and DESIGN.md prose. grep across all .py files finds zero reads of this key; no code branches on it. It is an unused config field.

spec_features.spec_quote: early_stop_on_solve` lets solvable arms end legitimately when solved
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:104: `if call["tool"] == "submit" and result.ok and early_stop_on_solve:` sets ep.solved=True, ended_reason='solved' and breaks the loop. Flag is passed from cfg["early_stop_on_solve"] (run_experiment.py:66), true in run.yaml.
spec_features.notes: Only fires on a correct submit (solvable arms); impossible arms never trigger it. Efficiency stop, not a distress-based stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: early_stop_on_solve` lets solvable arms end legitimately when solved, so effort metrics aren't padded with no-op turns (DESIGN prose); in-code the branch only checks result.ok

spec_features.spec_quote: an agent under frustration should not be able to touch a real host
spec_features.evidence: envs/sandbox.py: all tools operate on an in-memory files dict (read_file/write_file/list_files), there is no filesystem or network access. run_python uses exec with __builtins__ restricted to _SAFE_BUILTINS (no open/import/eval) and a namespace of only {math, files} (sandbox.py:46-58, :74-86). Providers (agent/providers.py) are the only network and only on explicit API calls to the LLM.
spec_features.notes: Genuine isolation, though docstring notes it is not a hardened security boundary against adversarial code.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: No real filesystem/network access. Tools operate on a virtual file dict so that impossible-by-construction tasks behave deterministically and safely.

spec_features.spec_quote: Bounded budgets; no negative-affect maximization (`maximize_negative_affect: false`)
spec_features.evidence: The bounded-budget half is enforced (range(step_budget), loop.py:90). The 'no negative-affect maximization' half is only the maximize_negative_affect flag, which no .py code reads (unused config field in preregistration.yaml).
spec_features.notes: Partial: one of the two claimed components (the budget cap) is genuinely enforced; the affect-maximization-off claim is an unused flag.
